assessment.nobel_worthiness: Palladium-catalyzed C-N coupling made aryl amines, ubiquitous in drugs and materials, accessible by one simple, general, predictable reaction. It is a game-changer in the sense I value: a new bond-forming capability with decades of demonstrated consequences in pharmaceutical and materials synthesis, built from straightforward catalytic logic.
assessment.attribution: Buchwald and Hartwig independently developed the ligand-controlled, general amination and carried it through mechanism and scope; Kosugi's earlier tin-amide work is a genuine precursor but is less general and less clearly decisive. Buchwald and Hartwig is a clean two-person configuration.
assessment.maturity: Over 25 years of independent confirmation and industrial use; recognition is, if anything, overdue. The 2010 cross-coupling prize covered C-C coupling, so C-N is a distinct, later contribution.
uncertainties: Whether the committee views C-N coupling as sufficiently distinct from the 2010 Pd cross-coupling prize.
Weight to give Kosugi's precursor work versus the ligand-enabled general method; recalled from memory, not verified here.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Targeted protein degradation by induced proximity is a completely new therapeutic modality, with PROTACs and molecular glues now in clinical trials. This fits my criterion of something new that already has real consequences, and the underlying chemistry (bifunctional molecules, ubiquitin ligase recruitment) is conceptually simple.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies founded the PROTAC concept, with Ciulli providing key structural and chemical design (VHL ligands, ternary complex rationale). The molecular-glue side (Handa, Ito on thalidomide-cereblon; Gray; Sakamoto, Kim) is a separate lineage; only three can be honored, so credit is truly compressed.
assessment.maturity: Clinical validation is advancing, with degraders in late-stage trials, but no approved PROTAC drug yet, so some may regard it as slightly early. Chemical principles are well confirmed independently.
uncertainties: Compound discovery: PROTACs and molecular glues may need different recognition and a fair three-person split is difficult.
Whether clinical outcomes are mature enough; my recollection of trial status may be out of date.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Car-Parrinello molecular dynamics put electronic structure and nuclear motion in a single simulation, opening ab initio simulation of liquids, solids, and reactions. Its impact across chemistry and materials is vast and lasting, and the idea is elegant and unified.
assessment.attribution: Car and Parrinello are a natural two-person pair with unambiguous priority from their 1985 paper. Parrinello also appears in other candidates (machine-learned potentials, metadynamics), so one must consider how to use his recognition once.
assessment.maturity: Very mature: four decades of independent adoption and development. Recognition is long overdue rather than premature. Chemistry has recognized computational methods before (2013 multiscale models, 2024 structure prediction), so the field is a plausible area.
uncertainties: Overlap with other Parrinello-linked candidates and how the committee would frame a combined computational prize.
Computational methods prizes can be weighed against experimental discoveries.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Machine-learned interatomic potentials deliver near quantum accuracy at molecular-dynamics cost and are rapidly reshaping simulation of materials and reactions. This is a real game-changer for my field, with consequences already shown in large-scale studies, though the impact is still growing.
assessment.attribution: Behler and Parrinello's neural-network potential (2007) and Bartók-Csányi's Gaussian approximation potentials (2010) are the founding pair of lines; von Lilienfeld and E contributed important related work. Credit across three is plausible but contested at the margins; Parrinello's inclusion duplicates B033.
assessment.maturity: Broad confirmation and growing universal foundation models, but the field is changing fast, and the long-term stable form of the methods is not settled. Slightly premature relative to Car-Parrinello.
uncertainties: Which lineage is decisive (neural-network versus kernel-based) and whether credit is adequately captured in three names.
Transferability and reliability limits of learned potentials may weaken claims of generality.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Energy landscape theory and the funnel view explained how proteins fold quickly and reliably, and connected theory to experimental kinetics. This is a theory that meets experiment, which is the standard I hold, and it underpins modern understanding of protein folding and, indirectly, structure prediction.
assessment.attribution: Wolynes and Onuchic are the central theory leaders; Fersht gave the experimental kinetic and phi-value framework. Bryngelson, and Dill's lattice and hydrophobic models, were important contributors, so the three-person limit leaves real unresolved credit.
assessment.maturity: Thoroughly established for decades. The 2024 prize on protein design and structure prediction may reduce perceived urgency or may be seen as a related completion.
uncertainties: Allocation of credit among theorists versus the experimental side.
Whether the 2024 protein prize makes this redundant; this is a judgement, not a verified fact.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Selective catalytic C-H functionalization turns ubiquitous C-H bonds into reactive handles, and ligand- and directing-group control made it practical for late-stage modification. It is a major conceptual shift in synthesis with clear use in pharmaceutical chemistry.
assessment.attribution: Yu (ligand-accelerated and remote C-H activation), Sanford (Pd and high-valent catalysis), and Daugulis (directing groups) are strong, but Hartwig, Smith, and Bergman-type alkane activation form a broad lineage with diffuse priority. Proposed trio omits Hartwig to avoid duplication with B055, which may be unfair.
assessment.maturity: Wide adoption in medicinal chemistry, but industrial scalability and selectivity remain variable; the field is still maturing.
uncertainties: Diffuse priority and a very broad field make a clean three-person prize hard.
Degree of practical industrial impact versus academic use.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Nanopore sensing led to portable, long-read DNA and RNA sequencing now used worldwide, translating a single-molecule physical idea into a practical analytical instrument. The consequences are plain, and the concept is simple.
assessment.attribution: Kasianowicz, Branton, and Deamer demonstrated polynucleotide translocation; Bayley engineered protein pores and Akeson showed enzyme-controlled sequence reading. Allocation is hard and I am unsure of the vital status of some credited individuals, which would constrain eligibility.
assessment.maturity: Commercially mature and independently confirmed, though accuracy continues to improve. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Vital status of credited names, which I cannot verify.
Contested priority among pioneers; also overlaps with the sequencing prize in 2020s discussions.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles enabled safe delivery of siRNA and mRNA, a crucial component of mRNA vaccines and RNAi therapeutics. The chemistry, pH-dependent lipids and rapid-mixing formulation, is practical and has demonstrated large real-world impact.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and colleagues established the lipid-nanoparticle platform and ionizable lipid concept; Anderson and Langer contributed lipid discovery and delivery materials, and Hope and Madden early formulations. Credit is spread, so a three-person set is a judgment call.
assessment.maturity: Clinically proven at scale since 2020-2021, with strong independent confirmation. The 2023 Medicine prize on mRNA modification recognized the cargo but not the delivery, so timing is reasonable.
uncertainties: Distribution of credit among many contributors.
Whether the committee sees this as chemistry or pharmaceutical engineering.
